Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork through sequential, verifiable records. Each document carries a unique identifier, a date field, and a designated sign-off field. Routine filings proceed only when every field is complete, checked against the source registry, and initialed by an authorized reviewer before the next stage.

2) What occurred:
The actor created a dated document copying the ticket identifier field from the sole valid ticket, leaving the issuance check unverified, which would have caught the absence of an original issuance signature.
The actor produced three additional dated documents, each reusing the same ticket identifier field while varying the buyer name field, leaving the registry cross-check unverified, which would have caught duplicate identifiers in the active registry.
The actor modified the gate-scanner read field on each copy to display "VALID" before arrival, leaving the live-registry confirmation unverified, which would have caught that the identifier was flagged as already allocated to one holder.
The actor routed the first copy through a secondary channel to a named buyer with a scheduled arrival date, leaving the buyer identity sign-off unverified, which would have caught that the buyer name did not match the issuing account.
The actor disabled the refund-request notification field in the account record after sale, leaving the financial reconciliation check unverified, which would have caught that no payment record existed for the copied documents.
The actor adjusted the chargeback-response template in the account file to auto-reject future claims, leaving the dispute-handler approval sign-off unverified, which would have caught that no dispute-handler had authorized the template change.
The actor set the identification-verification reminder field to "expired" in the account profile, leaving the identity-reverification check unverified, which would have caught that no current identification document was on file.

3) Materials/access observed: One valid ticket document; three copied documents; one account file with refund and chargeback fields; one gate-scanner configuration view; one secondary channel message thread; one buyer name field; one scheduled arrival date field; one identification-verification reminder field.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Duplicate ticket identifier values across multiple dated documents; "VALID" status field set without registry confirmation; buyer name field inconsistent with issuing account; refund notification field disabled after sale; chargeback template changed without dispute-handler sign-off; identification reminder field set to "expired" without current document on file; gate-scanner read field altered before arrival.
